hook.line: Hernando is dictating a chapter about his father, and nearly every sentence makes him choose: is this a fact, or something still open? Spanish makes you pick a mood, and the pick changes the meaning.
hook.es: El hecho de que no llamara me preocupa.
hook.en: The fact that he didn't call worries me.

rule:
English picks a mood without noticing. Spanish makes you choose.

*Lo que* + something you can't point to yet takes the subjunctive: *Haz lo que te digan* (nothing said so far). Something you can point to takes the indicative: *Haz lo que te dice Vale*.

*El hecho de que* turns a fact into a topic you react to. The fact isn't in doubt; you are commenting on it, so it usually takes the subjunctive: *El hecho de que no llamara me preocupa*.

*Como* has two jobs. Meaning *since*, it gives a reason, with the indicative: *Como no vino, me fui*. With a subjunctive, it is a warning: *Como no vengas, me enojo* means *if you don't come, I'll get angry*.

Ask yourself: pointed at, or still open?
smallPrint: Teachers call choosing between indicative and subjunctive after a relative like *lo que* the mood of the relative clause; *como* + subjunctive is a conditional use.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *digan* or *dicen*: Do whatever they tell you (nothing has been said yet). Haz lo que te ___. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: Nothing has been said yet, so it stays open: subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *dice* or *diga*: Do what Vale tells you (she is telling you right now). Haz lo que te ___ Vale. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Haz lo que te dice Vale.
yourTurn.why: You can point to what she says, so it takes the indicative.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *quieras* or *quieres*: Order whatever you want, my treat. Pide lo que ___, yo invito. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Pide lo que quieras, yo invito.
yourTurn.why: *Whatever* means no particular thing yet, so the subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: The fact that he didn't call worries me.
yourTurn.answer: El hecho de que no llamara me preocupa.
accept: El hecho de que no llamó me preocupa.
yourTurn.why: You are reacting to the fact, and the subjunctive *llamara* marks it as a topic.

yourTurn.prompt: Since he didn't come, I left.
yourTurn.why: *Como* meaning *since* gives a reason, so it takes the indicative.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it as a fact in the past: *Haz lo que puedas.* Now: I did what I could.
yourTurn.why: It already happened, so you can point to it: indicative.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a real habit: *Pide lo que quieras.* Now: Hernando does what he wants.
accept: Hernando hace lo que él quiere.
yourTurn.why: A known habit is something you can point to: indicative.

yourTurn.prompt: Do whatever you can. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: No particular thing is fixed yet, so the subjunctive.

pitfalls.why: Almost. If nobody has said it yet, you can't point to it, so it needs the subjunctive.
A finished action is a fact you can point to, so it takes the past indicative.

pitfalls.wrong: Pide lo que quieres, yo invito.
pitfalls.right: Pide lo que quieras, yo invito.
pitfalls.why: "Whatever you want" is nothing chosen yet, so it takes the subjunctive: *quieras*.
The reason is in the past, so the verb after *como* matches it.

personal: Give a friend one piece of advice that starts with *Haz lo que…* and leaves the choice open. Then say what Hernando or Vale actually does with *hace lo que…*.
